claims.text: Ultrafast pulsed-laser additive manufacturing of AlCrFeNiSi will reduce residual thermal stresses relative to conventional high-thermal-load additive manufacturing.
Ultrafast pulsed-laser additive manufacturing will improve the mechanical properties of AlCrFeNiSi components.
The predicted improvements arise from limiting overall thermal exposure during fabrication.
The AlCrFeNiSi powder has an as-atomized microstructure.
Femtosecond laser pulses minimize melt-pool lifetime.
Femtosecond laser pulses minimize overall heat accumulation.
The proposed processing window is applicable to miniature components with characteristic dimensions below 5 mm.
The process should be conducted in an inert atmosphere using femtosecond-range pulse durations.
Laser fluence can be tuned to produce melt pools approximately 10–50 µm in size.
The proposed regime will produce rapid solidification with minimal heat diffusion.
The intervention will produce an ultrafine-grained microstructure.
The intervention will produce a near-equilibrium microstructure with suppressed phase growth.
The refined microstructure will minimize residual thermal stresses.
Reduced cumulative thermal input limits thermal gradients.
Limiting thermal gradients reduces cooling-induced residual stresses.
Rapid solidification favors a homogeneous microstructure and improved mechanical integrity.
Ultrafast-processed components will have higher tensile strength than conventionally processed components.
Ultrafast-processed components will have higher hardness than conventionally processed components.
Conventional high-thermal-load additive manufacturing creates larger melt pools, higher residual stresses, and degraded mechanical properties.
The proposed benefits may not extend to components larger than 5 mm or to different alloy systems.

contradictions.description: The mediator is described as near-equilibrium, whereas the mechanism relies on ultrafast melting and rapid solidification, conditions normally associated with strongly nonequilibrium microstructure formation. No explanation reconciles these descriptions.
